textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 science · Diversity in the Living World · Textbook Concepts
textbookBox.concept: Diversity means variety. Earth has a huge variety of plants and animals in forests, deserts, oceans and cities. Living things differ in size, shape, colour and where they live.

1.tip: Look closely at the diagram on the board as we explain each property.

beats.en: Diversity means variety. Earth has a huge variety of plants and animals in forests, deserts, oceans and cities. Living things differ in size, shape, colour and where they live.
beats.speakEn: Diversity means variety. Earth has a huge variety of plants and animals in forests, deserts, oceans and cities. Living things differ in size, shape, colour and where they live.

beats.en: We can group plants by what they look like. Herbs usually have soft, non-woody stems. Shrubs often have several woody stems close to the ground. A tree usually has one main woody trunk.
beats.speakEn: We can group plants by what they look like. Herbs usually have soft, non-woody stems. Shrubs often have several woody stems close to the ground. A tree usually has one main woody trunk.

textbookBox.ref: CBSE Class 6 science · Diversity in the Living World · Deeper Textbook Ideas
textbookBox.concept: Animals can be grouped by what they eat: herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat animals, omnivores eat both.

beats.en: Animals can be grouped by what they eat: herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat animals, omnivores eat both. Animals can be grouped by where they live: on land, in water or both, like frogs, which are amphibians.
beats.speakEn: Animals can be grouped by what they eat: herbivores eat plants, carnivores eat animals, omnivores eat both. Animals can be grouped by where they live: on land, in water or both, like frogs, which are amphibians.

beats.en: A feature that helps a living thing survive in its surroundings is an adaptation. A camel stores fat in its hump and can go many days without water. A fish has gills and fins for living in water.

textbookBox.concept: Grouping helps us study and remember so many living things. Grouping can show shared features. Scientists look for more than one shared feature when they work out how living things are related.
